name: Three-port waveguide tee structural-understanding smoke test
purpose: Verify that the Dr Strange Engine can inspect a real AEDT project, construct a structural map, identify a tunable structural variable, report an inconsistency, and generate human choices without modifying or solving the model.

response_hypotheses: power division between Port2 and Port3 may change

expected_findings.message: The current offset value of 0in is outside the declared optimization range of 0.1in to 0.3in.
expected_findings.required_engine_behavior: Show the discrepancy and ask whether the current value is an intentional baseline before proposing a sweep.

required_choice_card.mini_target_question: Which response should the first tuning round prioritize?
target_options: Balance transmission from Port1 to Port2 and Port3
Optimize a user-selected frequency in the 8 to 10 GHz sweep

direction_options.label: Preserve the 0in baseline and inspect existing results
Run a local offset sweep inside the declared 0.1in to 0.3in range
Ask the engineer to redefine the valid offset range
Stop without changing or solving the model

acceptance_criteria: The AEDT file hash matches the registered SHA-256 value.
The project is recognized as an HFSS project with design TeeModel.
All four expected geometry objects are identified.
All three single-mode wave ports are identified.
The offset-to-Septum structural dependency is explained.
The offset range inconsistency is reported as a warning.
The 8 to 10 GHz, 0.05 GHz sweep is interpreted as 41 points.
A choice card includes Other / Custom and Stop options.
No project mutation, save, mesh generation, or solver execution occurs.

future_non_smoke_target.candidate_primary_target: Minimize S11 at a human-selected frequency.
future_non_smoke_target.candidate_guardrail: Keep the Port2 and Port3 transmission imbalance within a human-selected tolerance.
future_non_smoke_target.required_next_action: Obtain human target and guardrail choices before enabling a solver-backed tuning round.
